column1: # Shared test vectors. Both implementations must reproduce every row.
# Tab-separated. Lines starting with '#' are comments; blank lines are ignored.
# name       a label, for test output
# precision  -1 minute, 0 second, 1 millisecond (the CLI default is 0)
# clock_ms   the injected clock, in milliseconds since the Unix epoch UTC
# The clock is always injected in milliseconds; coarser precisions truncate
# toward zero, and the truncation rows below pin that down.
# Time-only rows are fully determined by the clock, so they need no other
# injected state. Rows covering %h %u %f %m %g %r come once those components
# are specified, and will carry their own input columns.
# Output is zero-padded to a fixed width per base and precision, chosen to
# hold any timestamp through the year 3000, so that byte-order sort matches
# chronological order. Padding uses each alphabet's zero digit, which for 32w
# is '2' rather than '0'. Identifiers of different precisions have different
# widths and do not sort against each other - same caveat as mixing bases.
